token encoding: assets are referenced, not tokenized: an asset manifest with `id, status (have|commissioning|tool|library|placeholder|n/a), files, licence, owner, brief`; DTCG has no asset type (L05 cross-lane note).
platform notes: app icons and favicons have platform size sets (Part H); fonts need app-embedding rights for native apps, not only web rights (Part H).
accessibility constraints: logos are exempt from contrast minimums but meaningful icons and images need text alternatives (L05).
default: (default + heuristic) Grouped checklist; fallback order: have it > commission a designer (with the generated brief) > open library with a compatible licence > named tool with its caveat > omit. Never present a generated identity asset as final.

title: Variant generation (how "show me options" works)
questions: (questions the designer answers) How many directions do you want to see? Which parts should vary (type, color, layout, motion)?
options:
- *Parameter shuffle with locks:* shadcn create, Realtime Colors (L16 Part D).
- *Concepts first, then renders, anti-convergence enforced:* gstack (3 default, up to 8; each variant differs in family, palette and layout) [S-L17-005].
- *Creative range dial:* Stitch SDK REFINE / EXPLORE / REIMAGINE with aspects (L16 C2).
- *Endless feed:* Variant (L16 C2).
visual effect: anti-convergence produces directions that feel like different teams made them; shuffle produces siblings [S-L17-005] [inferred].
depends on: brand inputs, memorable thing, any references.
affects: the chosen direction sets dial values for every foundation.
token encoding: each variant is a dial vector plus overrides; the chosen one becomes the token source; rejected ones are kept in the log.
platform notes: render variants on the target platform's real components (web and native previews differ) [inferred].
accessibility constraints: every variant must pass the contrast target before it is shown [inferred].
default: (default + heuristic) 3 concepts in text, confirm, render on real components with light and dark side by side; remix at block level; lock and shuffle for fine exploration afterwards.

title: Proposal framing (safe choices versus risks)
questions: (questions the designer answers) Which departures from the category do you want to take?
options: *Plain recommendation;* *options table without a recommendation;* *safe/risk split with gain and cost per risk* (gstack) [S-L17-004]; *three-layer synthesis* (convention, trend, first principles) [S-L17-003].
visual effect: the safe/risk split keeps most of the product conventional and concentrates distinctiveness in 2-3 places, which Anthropic's skill also recommends ("spend your boldness in one place") [S-L17-021].
depends on: research or references, brand inputs.
affects: where the Expression and Brand presence dials sit; which blocks carry the signature.
token encoding: `rationale: {safe: [...], risks: [{what, why, gain, cost}]}` in the decision log.
platform notes: on native platforms, risks usually belong in content and brand moments, not in system controls (L10) [inferred].
accessibility constraints: a risk may never break a hard rule (contrast, targets, reduced motion).
default: (default + heuristic) Always show the split; default to 2 risks, at least one tied to the memorable thing.

title: Anti-generic guardrails
questions: (questions the designer answers) How strict should the builder be about common AI-generated looks? Which rules do you want to waive?
options:
- *None:* accept whatever the model produces.
- *Hard bans:* gstack's banned faces and blacklist as absolute rules [S-L17-004].
- *Lint with ids, severity and waivers:* impeccable's 61 deterministic rules as a model [S-L17-020] [S-L17-011].
- *Model critique only:* a vision or LLM pass; gstack deferred this because vision misjudges some patterns [S-L17-011].
visual effect: lint with waivers removes accidental defaults (purple gradients, identical card grids, one radius everywhere) while allowing a chosen look, such as Inter for a dense tool [inferred].
depends on: direction and surface modes.
affects: critique stage, export lint rules.
token encoding: rule catalog with `id, severity, rationale, waived_by, reason` in the guardrails config.
platform notes: most rules are web-marketing tells; Operate surfaces and native apps need a smaller set [S-L17-007] [inferred].
accessibility constraints: accessibility rules are never waivable; taste rules are.
default: (default + heuristic) Lint with waivers, deterministic first, model critique second; taste rules warn, accessibility rules fail.

title: Pacing (where the model slows down)
questions: (questions the designer answers) How deep do you want to go (Quick, Standard, Expert)?
options: *Uniform* (every question equal); *depth modes only* (QUESTIONNAIRE); *fan-out weighted with decision classes* (slow on high fan-out and taste decisions, silent on mechanical ones) [S-L17-015].
visual effect: the person spends minutes on brand, platforms and direction and seconds on spacing steps, which is where the downstream effect is (decision-graph fan-out: DC-L06-02 15, DC-L10-01 12, DC-L15-01 12) [inferred from `synthesis/decision-graph.json`].
depends on: the decision graph, classification.
affects: stage length, which questions appear in Quick mode.
token encoding: per node `fan_out`, `class`, `min_mode`.
platform notes: multi-platform scope raises the weight of platform decisions (L10).
accessibility constraints: the accessibility target (Q-aud-03) is always asked in Standard and above even though its fan-out is modest, because it bounds many values [inferred].
default: (default + heuristic) Weight time by fan-out and class; never auto-decide an I block; auto-decide G blocks with visible defaults.

title: Coverage check and completeness scoring
questions: (questions the designer answers) Which open items are acceptable for now?
options: *Checklist of sections;* *per-block status over the ontology* (pending, default, decided, not applicable, awaiting asset); *0-10 per layer with "what a 10 looks like"* (gstack) [S-L17-006]; *A-F grades with weighted categories* (gstack live review) [S-L17-008].
visual effect: the person sees exactly what is missing; nothing is silently skipped (BRIEF requirement 5).
depends on: ontology, classification, hook statuses.
affects: export gate, team summary.
token encoding: coverage report generated from node statuses; waivers carry reasons.
platform notes: a block can be decided on one platform and pending on another; status is per platform where the node varies by platform [inferred].
accessibility constraints: unmet hard rules block "complete" status.
default: (default + heuristic) Per-block status plus a 0-10 score per layer with the gap in plain words; export allowed with a named remainder.

title: What the process records (for harmony and team communication)
questions: (questions the designer answers) Who else needs to understand these decisions?
options: *Tokens only;* *tokens + DESIGN.md* (gstack, Stitch) [S-L17-004] [S-L17-010]; *product context + DESIGN.md + tokens + decision log with provenance + asset manifest + coverage report* (recommended); *full docs site* (Part D tools).
visual effect: none on the product; on the team, a decision log in plain words lets engineers explain choices and lets the next session extend the system without drift (BRIEF requirements 9-10) [inferred].
depends on: every stage.
affects: later sessions (Stage 10), other agents reading the repo, team reviews.
token encoding: decision-log entries `{date, block, value, reason, source: default|reference|person|designer|asset, downstream}`; gstack's Decisions Log table is the minimal form [S-L17-004].
platform notes: none.
accessibility constraints: record the accessibility target and every waiver.
default: (default + heuristic) Always write all six records; the packaging of these files is L18's scope.

title: Preview substrate during the process
questions: (questions the designer answers) None; the builder chooses.
options: *Generated raster mockups* (gstack via an image model) [S-L17-012]; *real rendered components and screens from the current tokens* (L16 recommendation); *both: raster for mood exploration, rendered for decisions*.
visual effect: rendered previews are exact and editable; raster previews look richer early but cannot be measured, and their values have to be re-extracted by a vision model [S-L17-014] [inferred].
depends on: host capabilities (L18).
affects: accuracy of every decision made while looking at a preview.
token encoding: none.
platform notes: native previews need platform renderers or screenshots; web previews render directly [inferred].
accessibility constraints: only rendered previews can be checked for contrast and targets.
default: (default + heuristic) Rendered components for every decision; raster only for optional mood boards, labeled as such.

title: Approval gates
questions: (questions the designer answers) Do you approve this structure, this direction, these assets?
options: *No gates (one-shot generation);* *gates at structure, direction, assets* (site-soul-extractor, which calls skipping the direction gate its most repeated failure) [S-L17-023]; *gate per issue* (gstack plan review asks once per gap) [S-L17-006]; *final gate only for taste decisions* (gstack autoplan) [S-L17-015].
visual effect: gates prevent building a full system on a direction nobody chose [S-L17-023].
depends on: depth mode.
affects: cost of rework.
token encoding: gate records in the decision log.
platform notes: none.
accessibility constraints: none.
default: (default + heuristic) Three gates (block map and scope, direction, assets) plus a final taste-decision review; Quick mode keeps only the direction gate.

title: The per-block detail panel (how the builder teaches while editing)
block path: Builder > Guidance > Block detail panel (every G block; component pages extend DC-L08-23)
questions: (questions the designer answers) None; this is what the person sees beside every control.
options:
- *Value and live preview only:* most theme playgrounds (L16 Part D).
- *Props and stories only:* Storybook autodocs gives description, primary story with controls and a props table, but no usage guidance [S-L17-343].
- *NN/g record:* what it is, states, context of use, do's and don'ts, real-content example, content standard, code [S-L17-112] [S-L17-110] [S-L17-111].
- *Comparative guidance:* "use this when X, otherwise use Y", with a numeric threshold and the named alternative (NN/g dropdowns; designsystems.surf blueprints compare switch vs checkbox vs radio vs segmented control) [S-L17-117] [S-L17-306].
- *Agent-oriented guidelines:* Figma Make kit component files carry when-to-use, variant decision trees and correct/incorrect usage, in many short files [S-L17-200]; Figma notes agents may not know when to use a component without descriptions [S-L17-261].
visual effect: the panel turns each decision into a small lesson, so the person learns where a block belongs while choosing it (BRIEF requirement 3) [inferred].
depends on: the lane Decision Cards (defaults, options, systems that use them).
affects: generated docs, DESIGN.md prose, agent rule files, the team summary.
token encoding: per block `{what, use_when, avoid_when: [{condition, instead}], threshold, example, source_cards, downstream}` stored beside the tokens and exported into docs and agent files.
platform notes: thresholds and alternatives can differ by platform (for example sheet vs dialog on phones, L08); the panel shows the platform variant [inferred].
accessibility constraints: every panel lists the accessibility rule that bounds the block, with the check result.
default: (default + heuristic) Always show what it is, where to use, where not to (with the alternative and a threshold when one exists), a live preview in all modes, its source, and what else changes. Keep it short: NN/g's lean-team guidance favors precise over exhaustive docs [S-L17-113].

title: Primary delivery unit
questions: (questions the designer answers) What does a person install to get OpenDesigner into their AI? Does it need a server? Does it work offline?
options: (a) **Agent Skill folder** (SKILL.md + references + scripts + assets): loads in Claude app/Code/API, ChatGPT (via plugin) and Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI and ~40 more [S-L18-001, S-L18-203, S-L18-106]. (b) **MCP server first**: one visual implementation for Claude + ChatGPT + VS Code + Cursor, but needs hosting and gives nothing visual in terminal agents [S-L18-024, S-L18-044]. (c) **Custom GPT**: retiring 11 Dec 2026 [S-L18-118]. (d) **Standalone web app**: full control, but not "load into your own AI" (BRIEF req. 6). (e) **Project knowledge bundle** (ChatGPT/Claude Projects): zero install, weakest structure [S-L18-126].
visual effect: (a) text-first with host-native visuals where present; (b) the same widget UI in every chat host that renders MCP Apps; (d) the richest UI but outside the user's AI [inferred].
depends on: BRIEF requirements 6-7.
affects: DC-L18-02 to 07; build order (Part I).
token encoding: `skills/opendesigner/SKILL.md` with portable frontmatter only (`name`, `description`, `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`) [S-L18-003, S-L18-050].
platform notes: claude.ai needs code execution enabled; API skills have no network; ChatGPT web gets skills only inside plugins [S-L18-001, S-L18-106].
accessibility constraints: text fallback must be complete so screen-reader and terminal users lose nothing [inferred].
default: (default + heuristic) **(a) skill first, (b) MCP server second, (e) as a documented fallback, never (c).** Heuristic: "If you're explaining how to do something, that's a skill; if you need access to something, that's MCP" [S-L18-053].

title: Repo layout for multi-host discovery
questions: (questions the designer answers) Which folders must exist so each agent finds the skill and the instructions when the repo is cloned? Symlinks or copies?
options: (a) `skills/` source of truth + **generated real copies** in `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` (+ `.kiro/skills/` if wanted). (b) Symlinks `.claude/skills -> .agents/skills` (SSW's recommendation) [S-L18-258]. (c) Only `.agents/skills` (misses Claude Code, Cline, Kiro) [S-L18-212, S-L18-241, S-L18-234]. Instructions: (i) AGENTS.md canonical + `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` each containing `@AGENTS.md` [S-L18-211, S-L18-213]; (ii) AGENTS.md alone (Claude Code reads it only without CLAUDE.md, and not on Bedrock or older versions) [S-L18-036].
visual effect: none; this decides whether the interview starts at all in a given tool [inferred].
affects: release script, CI check that copies match, install docs.
token encoding: a `scripts/sync-skills` step that copies `skills/*` into discovery folders and fails CI on drift [inferred].
platform notes: Windows symlinks need admin or Developer Mode and Git checks them out as text files; Claude's Edit/Write refuse to write through symlinks; zip downloads and web uploads lose them [S-L18-211, S-L18-258, inferred]. Agent Plugins allows symlinks only inside the plugin root [S-L18-059].
accessibility constraints: n/a.
default: (default + heuristic) **(a) + (i).** Keep AGENTS.md under ~200 lines (Claude) and far under Codex's 32 KiB; it routes to the skill and data rather than repeating them [S-L18-329, S-L18-112, S-L18-134].

title: Plugin manifests and distribution channels
questions: (questions the designer answers) Through which stores and commands does each audience install it? Which manifests are needed?
options: (a) **Claude marketplace in the repo**: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` + `plugin.json`, installable with `/plugin marketplace add ckryptickunal/OpenDesigner` in Claude Code and via Customize > Plugins > Add marketplace in the Claude app; later a PR to `claude-plugins-official` [S-L18-004, S-L18-006, S-L18-007]. (b) **Agent Plugins `plugin.json`** at the root (+ optional `mcp.json`) for Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Copilot, Kiro; submit to the OpenAI plugin directory for ChatGPT web users [S-L18-059, S-L18-102, S-L18-103]. (c) **Release zip of the skill** for claude.ai upload and org provisioning [S-L18-002]. (d) **MCP registries** for the server (official registry, GitHub registry, Claude directory) [S-L18-246, S-L18-247, S-L18-028]. (e) **ChatGPT Project starter** (instructions + at most 5 knowledge files, to fit Free) [S-L18-126].
visual effect: none directly; ChatGPT web users only get plugin UI and skills through (b) + directory approval [S-L18-104].
affects: README install matrix; versioning (`version` in both manifests).
token encoding: Agent Plugins `plugin.json` needs `$schema` + `name` (1-64, lowercase, hyphens, periods); Claude `plugin.json` needs `name`; both find skills in `skills/` [S-L18-059, S-L18-004].
platform notes: No documented route lets a Plus/Pro ChatGPT web user install from GitHub directly [S-L18-104]; Codex IDE plugin support is contradictory [S-L18-107, S-L18-109]; the `anthropics/skills` repo is a working template for (a) [S-L18-034].
accessibility constraints: n/a.
default: (default + heuristic) **(a) + (b) + (c) at launch; (d) with the server; (e) as a Free-tier fallback.** One `skills/` folder, two manifests, one version number [inferred].

title: Knowledge format and chunking
questions: (questions the designer answers) How do 325 decision cards, the ontology and the questionnaire fit inside a model's context? Markdown or JSON?
options: (a) Ship the synthesis files as they are (QUESTIONNAIRE.md 267 KB, cards.json 826 KB, ontology.json 261 KB, measured on disk) and let the model read them. (b) **Chunk by stage and by card**: `references/stages/<nn>-<name>.md` (one screen each) + `data/*.json` indexes, loaded on demand. (c) Serve chunks only through MCP resources.
visual effect: (a) risks the model skimming or truncating; (b) keeps each step's facts in view [inferred].
depends on: `synthesis/QUESTIONNAIRE.md` stage structure; DC-L18-01.
affects: SKILL.md router, MCP resources, ChatGPT Project bundle.
token encoding: SKILL.md body under 5k tokens / 500 lines; references one level deep [S-L18-050]; JSON for data the model must not rewrite [S-L18-327, S-L18-332]; MCP results under Claude Code's 25k-token default [S-L18-037].
platform notes: ChatGPT Free Projects allow 5 files, so the Project bundle concatenates to <=5 files [S-L18-126]; Skills over MCP caps 512 files / 16 MiB per skill [S-L18-025].
accessibility constraints: n/a.
default: (default + heuristic) **(b), with (c) as a mirror when the server exists.** Rule: the model should never need more than one stage file plus the state file to ask the next question [inferred].

title: MCP server scope, hosting and auth
questions: (questions the designer answers) Should OpenDesigner run a server? Local or remote? Who pays for hosting? Does it need accounts?
options: (a) None (skill only). (b) **Remote, stateless, no-auth, read-only**: knowledge resources, pure generator tools, MCP Apps views, prompts (C2). (c) Local stdio package (`npx`, MCPB) for offline and for Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, VS Code [S-L18-049, S-L18-113]. (d) Remote with OAuth and saved projects.
visual effect: (b)/(c) unlock the widget interview in every MCP Apps host [S-L18-024].
affects: DC-L18-06/07; directory listings; security review.

platform notes: ChatGPT web cannot reach local servers except via Secure MCP Tunnel [S-L18-120]; Claude API connector is tools-only [S-L18-048]; the 2026-07-28 spec makes plain round-robin hosting possible [S-L18-022]; Cloudflare Workers supports it [S-L18-054].

title: Visual surface ladder and capability detection
questions: (questions the designer answers) On this host, right now, what is the best way to show a palette, a spacing scale or a component preview?
options: 1 OpenDesigner MCP App view (if its tools are present) [S-L18-011]; 2 Claude Design canvas when the user already uses it (hand-off, not control) [S-L18-029]; 3 host-native model-written HTML: Claude custom visuals, Claude/Claude Code artifacts, Codex desktop browser [S-L18-041, S-L18-043, S-L18-115]; 4 Figma or Paper canvas via their MCPs (L16); 5 local HTML file opened by the user; 6 host question tool (AskUserQuestion, `request_user_input`) [S-L18-304, S-L18-310]; 7 plain text with hex values and numbered options.
visual effect: 1-5 show the real effect of the choice; 6-7 describe it [inferred].
depends on: DC-L18-05; host (Part A).
affects: `assets/templates/*.html` (one template per foundation: palette, type scale, spacing ruler, radius/shape, elevation, motion, component sheet, options gallery) reused by rungs 1, 3 and 5 [inferred].
token encoding: each template reads a JSON payload (candidate tokens + labels) so the same file renders in any rung [inferred].
platform notes: Claude inline cards: max 2 actions, no dropdowns, carousels 3-8; fullscreen for editors [S-L18-017]; custom visuals are not on mobile [S-L18-041]; ChatGPT code-block previews have no return channel [S-L18-128].
accessibility constraints: every visual carries text equivalents (hex, contrast ratio, px values) so rung 7 is the same content [inferred]; honor host light/dark tokens for chrome [S-L18-017].
default: (default + heuristic) detect from the tools the model can see, pick the highest rung available, and say which rung is in use. Never block the interview on a visual [inferred].

title: How a visual choice returns to the model
questions: (questions the designer answers) After the user clicks a swatch, how does the model learn it, reliably and without retyping?
options: (a) MCP Apps `ui/message` (visible chat turn) or `tools/call` (`od_record_decision`) [S-L18-011]; (b) `ui/update-model-context` (silent context update) [S-L18-011]; (c) custom-visual click-to-prompt [S-L18-041]; (d) "Copy as prompt" string, e.g. `OD:set color.brand.seed=#3B5BDB` [S-L18-043]; (e) artifact comments sent to Claude (Team/Ent) [S-L18-043]; (f) Codex browser element comments [S-L18-115]; (g) typed reply.

title: What carries color on a screen
block path: Foundations > Color > Palette character > Where the color on a screen comes from
questions: (questions the designer answers) On a normal screen, what should be in color: the buttons, the data, the pictures, or only the things that changed? If the brand is black and white, is there any color at all? Should dashboards and marketing pages follow the same rule as app screens?
options:
- **Accent on actions** (the current `accent` and `strict` defaults): the accent marks the main action, links, the selected item and status. Linear is recognized by its blue-purple and Supabase by its bright green [S-L19-039]. In a nav bar, active states are a good place to add a pop of brand color [S-L19-075].
- **Ink (neutral brand):** black, white and grays carry the interface, the main button is near-black, and color appears only where meaning needs it. Vercel is roughly 90% black, 8% white and 2% red, yet build success, failure and progress still show in color [S-L19-039]. Steve Schoger swapped every use of an AI-picked emerald accent for gray 950 to keep a marketing page neutral [S-L19-103]. Polaris uses a black brand (DC-L01-08, DC-L01-10).
- **Data-led (dashboards):** controls stay neutral and the color comes from the data: micro charts on KPIs instead of colored buttons and icons [S-L19-061], a red icon in a chip for an urgent action, not color "sprinkled in to look nice" [S-L19-056].
- **Imagery-led (marketing pages):** the color pops come from the product visuals, which lets the buttons be white; a weak page puts its accent on everything that will take it [S-L19-072]. One redesign shows its bright orange accent only on the call to action's hover so it never overpowers the page [S-L19-065] (one video).
- **60-30-10 as a rule:** rejected for product UI, where screens can be almost entirely neutral [S-L19-039]; kept only as a loose balance check by the same creator's earlier video [S-L19-051]. This agrees with DC-L15-03 and DC-L15-06 (folk wisdom, soft check).
visual effect: Accent on actions reads as "color means click here", focused and calm (DC-L01-08). Ink reads premium, minimal and content-first (DC-L01-08's reading of Polaris), and status colors stand out hardest because nothing else is colored [inferred]. Data-led makes the numbers draw the eye while the interface recedes [inferred]. Imagery-led gives a more vibrant page with quiet controls [S-L19-072], where the screenshots do the talking [inferred].
depends on: Q-color-01 (brand input), Q-scope-01 (which surfaces the product has: app, dashboard, marketing), Q-color-03 (how colorful).
affects: `color.bg.action.primary` and its hover and pressed states (accent step or neutral ink), `color.text.link`, `color.bg.accent.*`, `color.chart.*`, icon color (Q-icon-05), nav active state, chips (chips almost never take the primary call-to-action color [S-L19-075]).
token encoding: no new tokens. `color.bg.action.primary` ($type color) aliases the accent solid step, or the neutral text step for ink, which is what the engine's monochrome scheme already does ("Buttons use near-black ink; color is kept for status, links and focus", engine.py). A per-surface accent budget can live in lint config under `$extensions` [inferred].
platform notes: The sources give none. Apple's one-accent guidance and "don't color several control backgrounds" are in DC-L01-08.
accessibility constraints: Meaning never rides on color alone (WCAG 1.4.1, DC-L01-23): a state that turns colored also needs an icon, a text change or a shape. Status icons need 3:1 and status text 4.5:1 against their surface (DC-L01-15). A near-black ink button with white text is about 17:1 [inferred].
default: (default + heuristic) Default: accent on actions for app screens (confirms Q-color-02 `accent` and Q-color-05 `strict`), data-led for dashboard views, imagery-led for marketing pages only when the team has product visuals to show (otherwise the current `moderate` for marketing stays), and ink when the brand is black and white. Heuristic: keep defaults gray and give color to what changed, what needs action, or what the data says: a checkbox is plain when off and gets fill, color and a checkmark when on; in a menu the only blue item is the resubscribe prompt [S-L19-080]; icons in app chrome stay uncolored except for status [S-L19-051], while marketing feature icons and icons in dense data rows may carry color on purpose [S-L19-061] [S-L19-062] [S-L19-082]. The semantic layer is never switched off, even in ink: destructive actions stay red whatever the brand ([S-L19-039] [S-L19-051]; a third video says "preferably red" [S-L19-057]), which is why red and green are often in a brand's palette even when they are not brand colors [S-L19-051].
maps to:
- Q-color-05: keeps its options and its default ("strict for app surfaces, moderate for marketing"); adds `data-led` as a named variant of `strict` for dashboard views and `imagery-led` as a variant of `moderate` for marketing pages that have product visuals, so this refines the default rather than replacing it; new heuristic "defaults gray, color marks change, action or data". Imagery-led is close to Q-color-02's existing `content-layer` (brand color lives in the content), and ink to Q-color-02 `neutral-first` plus Q-color-03 `monochrome` [inferred], so no new Q-color-02 option is needed.
- Q-color-02: confirms default `accent`; visual sample: Vercel's near-monochrome console with colored build statuses, and a menu whose only blue item is the resubscribe prompt [S-L19-080].
- Q-color-03: visual sample for `monochrome`: Vercel and Schoger's gray 950 page [S-L19-039] [S-L19-103]; new Use/avoid line: "monochrome never removes status colors" (confirms what the engine already does).
impact now / as it grows:
- Accent on actions: now, one hue to manage and a clear "clickable" signal. As it grows, every new feature competes for the same accent, so the emphasis budget has to be enforced (DC-L15-03).
- Ink: now, the quickest route to a polished look, with brand recognition carried by type and logo. As it grows, adding a brand hue later means re-deciding every primary button, while status colors stay stable.
- Data-led: now, dashboards need a chart palette (DC-L19-10) from day one. As it grows, more metrics and statuses need a categorical palette and color-blind cues.
- Imagery-led: now, it depends on having good product visuals (an asset only the team can supply). As it grows, every new page needs curated visuals, and stale screenshots drain the page of color.
standards: STD-visual-details-29 (the most important thing is the most obvious), STD-visual-details-25 (neutral grays and one accent when prototyping with no project tokens), STD-process-review-taste-37 (prototype variants that differ only in accent color are not real variants).

title: Light-mode page and card arrangement
questions: (questions the designer answers) In light mode, are cards lighter than the page (white cards on an off-white page) or darker than it (tinted cards on a white page)? How white is the page? How much darker is the sidebar or app frame?
options:
- **Cards lighter than the page:** the page sits just below white and the cards are pure white, as in Vercel (page about 98% white) [S-L19-039]. If cards are pure white, the page should not be (one video) [S-L19-039]. This is what the engine already generates in its default (non-tonal) model: page on neutral step 1, raised surfaces on white (engine.py surface mapping).
- **Cards darker than the page:** a pure white page with cards darker than it, often the same color as the sidebar, as in Notion (page 100% white) [S-L19-039].
- **Monochromatic layers:** stacked shades of one color, as in Supabase [S-L19-039]; the video names this option without describing it.
- **Alternating layers** (existing Q-color-14 option): Carbon's White and Gray 10 (DC-L01-13).
- **Reversed small features:** for small elements such as a search bar, swap the usual background and foreground, as Dribbble does [S-L19-051].
- Real page values: Linear 99%, Notion 100%, Vercel 98% white, so pure white is acceptable [S-L19-039]. The app frame or sidebar is a slightly darker anchor and needs only a very small shift because it is large (Mercury adds 2% blue) [S-L19-039]. A neutral gray background with a white or very light foreground is the general starting point [S-L19-051].
visual effect: Cards lighter: crisp, cards come forward, a dashboard feel (Vercel) [inferred]. Cards darker: airy and document-like, cards recede into panels (Notion) [inferred]. Monochromatic layers: soft and tonal [inferred]. Alternating: crisp, grid-like enterprise (DC-L01-13). Cards on a light page with no edge look washed out, and a subtle shadow alone is only slightly better [S-L19-039], so the edge decision (DC-L19-09) comes with this one.
depends on: Q-color-09 (gray tint), Q-color-14 (layer model), Q-color-10 (gray steps), Q-depth-01 (edge or shadow).
affects: `color.surface.base`, `color.surface.raised`, `color.surface.sunken`, the navigation surface, `color.bg.neutral.subtle`; cards, sidebars, popovers, wells; whether cards need a border ring.
token encoding: $type color. Cards lighter: `color.surface.base` = `{color.neutral.light.1}`, `color.surface.raised` = `{color.white}`. Cards darker: `color.surface.base` = `{color.white}`, `color.surface.raised` = `{color.neutral.light.2}` and the sidebar on the same step [inferred].
platform notes: The sources give none. iOS's system and grouped background sets are the platform's own version of this choice (DC-L01-13) [inferred].
accessibility constraints: Surface tones are decorative and need no ratio, but an interactive card defined only by tone needs a 3:1 boundary (WCAG 1.4.11, DC-L01-13). A 98% page against a white card is about 1.04:1, far too little to see an edge without a ring or border [inferred]. Text must pass 4.5:1 on every surface it sits on.
default: (default + heuristic) Default: cards lighter than the page (confirms the engine's current output). Offer cards darker for document, note and editor products [inferred from the Notion example]. Heuristic: never make both the page and the cards pure white (one video); make the frame or sidebar a slightly darker anchor, only one small step darker [S-L19-039]; if two surfaces are meant to differ, make the difference visible [S-L19-075]. The neutral budget in [S-L19-039] (about four background layers, at least one and often two strokes, and about three text colors for a product, before hover states; three to five neutrals for a landing page) fits within the engine's four surfaces, three border strengths and three text levels and within Q-color-10's default of 12 to 13 solid neutrals [inferred].
maps to:
- Q-color-14: keeps `role-tiers` as the default; adds a light-mode sub-choice under it, `cards-lighter` (default, which is the engine's current output) or `cards-darker`, because the existing options name the layers but do not say which way light-mode cards go; visual sample: one dashboard shown Vercel-style (white cards on a 98% page), Notion-style (darker cards on white) and Supabase-style (monochromatic layers), with the dark column showing lighter-when-higher (confirms the current dark default).
- Q-color-10: confirms default; new heuristic that a marketing-only system uses only three to five of its neutrals.
impact now / as it grows:
- Cards lighter: now, cards need an edge (ring or shadow) to avoid looking washed out. As it grows, nested cards need another near-white step, and the page tint becomes the thing that separates too many layers.
- Cards darker: now, a white page reads open and calm. As it grows, each nested panel steps darker, and text contrast on the darkest panel needs a check.
- Monochromatic layers: now, a soft branded feel. As it grows, status and chart colors must be checked against tinted layers (Q-color-09 warns strong tints make status colors look off).
standards: STD-visual-details-14 (separate surfaces with a semi-transparent shadow rather than an opaque border), STD-visual-details-17 (darker, heavier materials for structural regions such as sidebars, which matches the darker frame anchor [inferred]), STD-visual-details-24.

title: How much hue the grays and backgrounds carry
block path: Foundations > Color > Neutrals > Tint strength in both modes
questions: (questions the designer answers) Should the background be plain white or black, a barely tinted gray, or a clear wash of the brand color? Should the dark background be a neutral near-black, a blue-black, or a deep brand color? If you already have a product, which gray family does it use?
options:
- **Pure:** zero chroma. Pure white is acceptable [S-L19-039]. Schoger switched a generated page from slate to neutral grays because the product screenshot used neutral grays [S-L19-103].
- **Hue-matched, slight** (the current default, OKLCH chroma about 0.01 to 0.03 at mid steps, DC-L01-06): off-whites in light mode and bluish blacks in dark mode signal a more experienced designer [S-L19-057]; a hint of the brand hue in the neutral gray, and Headspace's orange tint behind cards [S-L19-051]; Mercury's 2% blue sidebar [S-L19-039]. Primer's blue-tinted #0D1117 is the research example (DC-L01-19).
- **Accent wash (new):** the background is a very light or very dark version of the accent. GitHub uses a really dark blue instead of pure black; a site captioned "Studio rubric" uses a very light orange; as a shortcut, Tailwind's 50 as the light background with its 500 as the accent, or its 950 as the dark background with its 300 as the primary [S-L19-070]. One video; its claim that the pairs work for every Tailwind color comes with no contrast check.
- **Deep-colored dark only:** light mode stays near-neutral while the dark base takes a deep hue: deep purples, reds or greens, not only navy or gray [S-L19-052]; a background gradient of two brand colors, darkened, for a dark mode that lacks color (Gemini's baby blue and pink) [S-L19-082].
- **Cool or warm** (existing options): unchanged.
visual effect: Pure: technical, never competes with photos, data or screenshots (DC-L01-06). Hue-matched: of a piece with the brand (DC-L01-06), the "experienced designer" look [S-L19-057]. Accent wash: strongly branded, the whole page carries color, less neutral [inferred]. Deep-colored dark: moody and distinctive; the dark mode becomes a brand moment [inferred].
depends on: Q-color-01 (seed hue), Q-color-03 (how colorful), Q-color-21 (how dark), the project's existing tokens.
affects: every neutral ramp, surface, border and text token in both modes; how status and chart colors read; screenshots placed on marketing pages.
token encoding: the engine's `color.neutral.tint.oklch` parameter carries chroma and hue per mode; accent wash makes the surface tokens alias the accent ramp's lightest steps in light and darkest steps in dark ($type color) [inferred].
platform notes: The sources give none. Apple system grays are defined per appearance and should not be hard-coded (DC-L01-06).
accessibility constraints: A tint shifts luminance only slightly, but text steps must be re-checked after tinting (DC-L01-06). Strong tints can make status colors look off (Q-color-09's avoid line). With an accent wash, accent text or buttons sit on their own hue, so the 500-on-50 and 300-on-950 pairs must pass the contrast matrix; the source did not check them [S-L19-070].
default: (default + heuristic) Default: keep hue-matched (confirms DC-L01-06, now supported by [S-L19-039] [S-L19-051] [S-L19-057]; [S-L19-070] goes further, to an accent-colored background). Use pure when the product shows photos or data, or when a marketing site must match an existing product that uses neutral grays. Offer accent wash and deep-colored dark as expressive options, each with a status-color check. Heuristic: match the gray family the product already uses [S-L19-103], which is also what STD-visual-details-26 asks (extend existing tokens, never a parallel set) [inferred link]. No source here recommends pure black as the dark base [S-L19-052] [S-L19-057] [S-L19-070], which confirms Q-color-21's `near-black` default.
maps to:
- Q-color-09: new option `accent-wash`; new heuristic "match the gray family the product already uses", pre-filled from Q-ref-01 or an extraction; visual sample: pure black against a GitHub-style blue-black, Headspace-style orange-tinted cards, and a Tailwind 50/500 pair.
- Q-color-21: new option `tinted-deep` (the dark base takes a deep brand or chosen hue) with an automatic status-color check; confirms the `near-black` default (the stage already notes that `black` smears and halates on OLED).
impact now / as it grows:
- Pure: now, safe with any content. As it grows, adding or changing a brand barely touches the grays.
- Hue-matched: now, cohesive. As it grows, a brand hue change re-tints every gray, so the tint needs one alias point (the engine parameter).
- Accent wash: now, very branded. As it grows, a second brand or theme means redoing every surface, status colors must be re-checked against the wash, and text contrast has less headroom.
- Deep-colored dark: now, a distinctive dark mode. As it grows, every new status or chart color has to be checked on the colored base.
standards: STD-visual-details-26 (reuse and extend existing tokens), STD-visual-details-25 (neutral grays when prototyping with no project), STD-visual-details-24 (a light and a dark value per role).

title: Spacing between dark-mode background shades
block path: Foundations > Color > Modes > Dark neutral step spacing
questions: (questions the designer answers) When we build the dark palette, how far apart should the dark background shades be so the page, cards, sidebars and popovers still look different? Should the dark steps simply mirror the light ones?
options:
- **Reflect the light steps:** rejected by the sources. If you just reflect the light palette, the background elements lose all their distinction [S-L19-039]; inverting is "not awful, but certainly not ideal" [S-L19-051]; light and dark should not be exact opposites [S-L19-067] (its captions are muddled; this is the analysis's reading).
- **Double the distance:** light background steps about 2% white apart become 4 to 6% in dark, because dark colors look more alike [S-L19-039]. Per dark card layer, raise HSB brightness by about 4 to 6 and lower saturation by 10 to 20, repeating for each layer [S-L19-070]. The two videos (both by the same creator) agree on the size of the step, and so does existing research: DC-L04-13 gives 3 to 5% lightness steps in dark.

- **What the engine does today** [inferred, worked out from the constants in engine.py for a pure gray: dark step 1 luminance 0.0075, dark step 7 at 2.0:1, light step 1 at 1.02:1 and light step 7 at 1.65:1 against white, steps 2 to 6 evenly spaced in OKLCH lightness]: dark neutral steps 1 to 4 come out near #151515, #1d1d1d, #252525, #2d2d2d, about 3.1% apart, below the videos' 4 to 6%. The dark surfaces use steps 1 (sunken), 2 (page), 3 (raised) and 4 (overlay). The light neutral steps 1 to 3 come out near #fdfdfd, #f4f4f4, #ebebeb, about 3.5% apart, but the light page (step 1) and its white cards differ by less than 1%, so the gap the videos ask to double is already narrow in light.
visual effect: Reflected: flat and muddy, cards melt into the page. Doubled: surfaces stay distinct and the dark mode looks "enterprise-grade" [S-L19-039]. Very wide steps (Carbon): strongly zoned, less subtle [inferred].
depends on: Q-color-16 (separate dark neutral ramps), Q-color-21 (base darkness), Q-color-14 (how many layers).
affects: dark values of `color.surface.*`, `color.bg.neutral.subtle` and its hover and pressed states, borders, popovers and menus.
token encoding: dark primitives `color.neutral.dark.1` to `.12` ($type color); semantic dark aliases such as `color.surface.raised` = `{color.neutral.dark.3}`; the gap can be a generator parameter under `$extensions` [inferred].

Wider gaps lift the top surface toward mid-gray, which lowers the contrast of light text on it, so text must still pass 4.5:1 on the lightest dark surface it sits on [inferred]. The engine already checks dark text against the lighter dark steps.
default: (default + heuristic) Default: adjacent dark surface tiers at least about 4% brightness apart, and never closer in dark than the same tiers are in light [S-L19-039] [S-L19-070], within the 2.7 to 6.3% range real systems use. Heuristic: if you have to squint to see that two dark surfaces differ, double the gap (a visible difference is the point, [S-L19-075]).

- Q-color-16: new heuristic "double the distance for dark backgrounds"; visual sample: the same dark dashboard with reflected light steps (cards vanish) and with doubled steps.

title: How raised surfaces stand out in dark mode
block path: Foundations > Color > Modes > Dark elevation cues
questions: (questions the designer answers) In dark mode, should a card stand out by being lighter, by an outline, or by both? How bright should dark-mode borders be?
options:
- **Lighter fill:** surfaces always get lighter as they rise [S-L19-039]; dark mode doesn't have shadows the way light mode does, so a card is lighter than the background [S-L19-052]; a dark background reads as farther back than lighter cards [S-L19-085]; layered HSB steps [S-L19-070]. Agrees with DC-L01-13 and DC-L04-13.
- **Border only:** a raised element defined by just a border, like a search bar [S-L19-039]. One designer prefers outlined cards in dark and filled cards in light, as taste ("totally up to you") [S-L19-047].
- **Fill plus brightened border:** brighten the borders and the main card, because dark colors must differ more to be seen [S-L19-051]; brighten any borders [S-L19-039].
- **Softened border:** a light card border had "a bit too much contrast" in dark mode, so it was lowered [S-L19-052]. This differs from the "brighten" advice.
- **Frosted glass:** if a dark design still lacks something, add frosted glass to the cards and the colored background [S-L19-085] (one video).
- **Shadows:** DC-L04-12 keeps shadows in dark (double the alpha, add a 1px light edge ring on overlays); the videos lean on lighter surfaces instead [S-L19-052] [S-L19-070].
visual effect: Lighter fill: soft and dimensional, as if lit from the front (Atlassian's reading in DC-L04-13). Border only: crisp, technical, line-drawn (a developer-tool feel) [inferred]. Fill plus border: the most separation, but busy if borders are too bright [inferred]. Glass: expressive and modern [inferred].
depends on: DC-L19-04 (step spacing), Q-color-14, Q-depth-01, Q-depth-04 (glass).
affects: dark values of `color.surface.raised`, `color.surface.overlay`, `color.border.subtle` and `color.border.default`, and `color.shadow.ring`; cards, popovers, menus, search fields.
token encoding: $type color for the dark border and surface values; `color.shadow.ring` (the engine already uses a ring at 10% alpha in light and 12% in dark) inside the $type shadow of overlays.
platform notes: The sources give none.
accessibility constraints: An input's boundary must stay 3:1 even when decorative borders are softened (DC-L01-16). Forced colors keeps borders and drops fills and shadows, so border-based options survive it (DC-L01-20). Glass needs the solid fallback under reduced transparency.
default: (default + heuristic) Default: lighter fill plus a subtle see-through light edge in dark (a low-alpha ring, as in DC-L19-09, rather than an opaque line, which follows STD-visual-details-14). The edge sits brighter than an inverted light palette would give it [S-L19-039] [S-L19-051] but not so bright that it gives the card too much contrast [S-L19-052]; this reconciles the two camps [inferred]. Overlays keep DC-L04-12's edge ring. Heuristic: if a dark border is the first thing you notice on a card, lower it [inferred, after the source's shadow rule of the same shape [S-L19-052]].
maps to:
- Q-color-14: confirms the dark default ("dark mode with lighter tones"); visual sample in the dark column: a card raised by fill, a search bar raised by border only, and a card with both.
- Q-color-23: new heuristic for dark borders (brighter than an inverted palette gives, never so bright that the card gets too much contrast [S-L19-052]); visual sample: a dark card whose too-bright border is lowered and whose chip is dimmed [S-L19-052].

title: Which shade of the accent does each job, in light and dark
block path: Foundations > Color > Ramps > Step jobs per mode
questions: (questions the designer answers) Which shade of the brand color is the main button, the hover and the link? Which shades take over in dark mode? What happens to bright chips and the logo in dark mode?
options:
- **Light mode (50 to 950 numbering):** main color at 500 or 600, hover at 700, links at 400 or 500 [S-L19-039]. Shortcut: Tailwind's 50 as a light background with its 500 as the accent [S-L19-070].
- **Dark mode:** primary at 300 or 400, hover at 400 or 500 [S-L19-039]; Tailwind's 300 as primary on its 950 [S-L19-070]; over-saturated primaries replaced with lighter versions [S-L19-085]. This agrees with Material (primary 40 becomes 80) and Atlassian (700 in light is 400 in dark) in DC-L01-18, and with "accents one or two steps lighter and lower in chroma" in DC-L01-19. Counter-example: Radix keeps its solid step the same in both modes (DC-L01-18).
- **Chips and tinted fills in dark:** a chip that is far too bright gets its saturation and brightness dimmed, with the treatment flipped for its text to keep hierarchy [S-L19-052] (read as a dim tinted fill with a bright label of the same hue [inferred]). The logo is desaturated a touch [S-L19-051] (one video each).
- **By number or by contrast:** the engine picks each step by contrast (the solid step reaches the text minimum with its on-color, links use a text step), which is the Q-color-07 and Q-color-08 default. In Tailwind, the same number differs in lightness across hues (at 500, blue is L 62.3% and amber L 76.9%, DC-L01-03).
visual effect: A 500 to 600 main in light gives a confident, saturated button [inferred]. A 300 to 400 main in dark is softer with less glare (desaturated dark accents avoid neon vibration, DC-L01-19). Saturated chips in dark look far too bright [S-L19-052]; dimmed chips with bright labels look calm and still readable [inferred].
depends on: Q-color-07 (how ramps are built), Q-color-08 (step count and numbering), Q-color-16 (dark mapping), Q-color-20 (states).
affects: `color.bg.action.primary` and its hover and pressed states, `color.text.link`, `color.text.on-action`, `color.bg.accent.subtle` and `.bold`, status subtle fills (`color.bg.success.subtle` and similar); chips, badges, the dark logo asset.
token encoding: per-mode semantic aliases, for example `color.bg.action.primary` = `{color.accent.light.9}` in light and `{color.accent.dark.9}` in dark ($type color); a label map from the 12-step jobs to 50 to 950 names for exports [inferred].
platform notes: Material's tone reassignment is the Android version (DC-L01-18); the sources give nothing platform-specific.
accessibility constraints: Pick steps by contrast, not by number: a link at "400 or 500" can be too light for 4.5:1 body text on white on many hues [inferred, consistent with DC-L01-03's lightness spread]. Dark primaries at 300 to 400 usually carry dark text (the Material 80/20 pattern the engine follows). Logos are exempt from contrast rules (DC-L01-09).
default: (default + heuristic) Default: confirms the contrast-indexed steps and Q-color-21's "accents one or two steps lighter and lower in chroma in dark". Heuristic for people who think in 50 to 950 numbers: main at 500 to 600, hover at 700 and links at 400 to 500 in light, and main at 300 to 400 in dark, is a starting map, and the contrast matrix has the final say. New: in dark mode, subtle levels are a dim, low-chroma fill with a bright label [S-L19-052], of the same hue [inferred reading]; ask for a dark-mode logo or apply a slight desaturation [S-L19-051].
maps to:
- Q-color-08: visual sample: the ramp strip labeled with each job in both numberings (1 to 12 and 50 to 950), in light and dark.
- Q-color-13: new heuristic for dark subtle levels (dim fill, bright same-hue label).
- Q-color-21: confirms the default (accents lighter and lower in chroma in dark).
- Logo asset hook: ask for a dark-mode logo variant, or desaturate slightly [inferred].

- By number: now, easy to talk about with designers. As it grows, new hues break the pattern (a yellow 500 is much lighter than a blue 500), so contrast-picked steps stay steadier as hues are added.

standards: STD-visual-details-24, STD-visual-details-26.

title: Which way colors move on hover and press
block path: Foundations > Color > States > Direction of state changes
questions: (questions the designer answers) When you hover or press a button, does its color get lighter or darker? Is that the same in dark mode? What does disabled look like, and what happens on touch screens with no hover?
options:
- **Toward more contrast** (the current default, DC-L01-17): hover one step and pressed two steps toward more contrast with the surface. The engine prefers darker states in light and lighter states in dark (engine.py `fit_states`).
- **Always a darker step:** hover steps to 700 from a 500 or 600 main in light, and to 400 or 500 from a 300 or 400 main in dark [S-L19-039]. In dark this moves toward less contrast with the surface [inferred], so it differs from DC-L01-17 in dark mode.
- **Lighter hover, darker press:** hover slightly lighter or brighter, press slightly darker [S-L19-051] (the source names no mode, so it reads as a general rule); Windows also lightens on interaction (DC-L01-17). In light mode this differs from DC-L01-17 for hover; in dark mode it agrees [inferred].
- **Disabled:** desaturate the color unless it is already gray; a light gray fill with white text reads as disabled in light and dark [S-L19-051]. Graying a button right after it is pressed shows the next screen is coming [S-L19-045] (a loading cue, not disabled).
- **Touch:** mobile has no hover, so tappable elements rely on a slightly darker press [S-L19-051].
visual effect: Toward more contrast: like pressing into paper on light surfaces and like lighting up on dark ones (DC-L01-17's reading) [inferred]. Always darker: a consistent pressed-into-paper feel, but in dark mode the button dims on hover [inferred]. Lighter hover: the button brightens on hover, and the darker press feels like pressing into something [S-L19-051].
depends on: DC-L19-06 (step jobs), Q-color-20 (steps or overlays), Q-plat-01 (touch).
affects: `color.bg.action.primary-hover` and `-pressed`, `color.bg.neutral.subtle-hover` and `-pressed`, `color.bg.accent.bold-hover` and `-pressed`, `color.bg.disabled`, `color.text.disabled`.
token encoding: the existing per-state tokens ($type color); the direction rule as a generator setting under `$extensions` [inferred].
platform notes: On the web, hover rules live inside `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and every tappable element gets its own `:active` state (STD-mobile-touch-21, STD-mobile-touch-03), which is the code form of "mobile relies on press" [S-L19-051].
accessibility constraints: Hover fills need no contrast minimum, but the label must still pass 4.5:1 on hover and pressed fills (DC-L01-17; the engine keeps on-text at the text minimum). Disabled is exempt from contrast, so it must not be the only way to tell that an action is unavailable when that matters [inferred]. The engine's minimum state differences (1.15:1 for hover, 1.3:1 for pressed) keep states visible.
default: (default + heuristic) Default: keep toward more contrast, because it is the only rule of the three that stays visible in both modes [inferred]. Record [S-L19-039]'s dark hover and [S-L19-051]'s light hover as disagreements with DC-L01-17, not overrides. Heuristic: press always moves further than hover, in the same direction; on touch-first products, design the press state first.
maps to:
- Q-color-20: new sub-choice at zoom 3, "direction": `toward-contrast` (default), `always-darker`, `lighter-hover`; visual sample: one button in light and dark with each direction, hover and press side by side.
- Q-state-04: visual sample for disabled: a light gray fill with a white label in both modes [S-L19-051].
impact now / as it grows:
- Toward more contrast: now, visible states everywhere. As it grows, new colors inherit the rule automatically.
- Always darker: now, simple to explain. As it grows, dark-mode hovers on new components drift toward the surface and can vanish.
- Lighter hover: now, a glowing feel. As it grows, light solids such as yellow lose their hover in light mode because they are already close to white [inferred].
standards: STD-easing-duration-01 (a hover or color change animates with `ease`), STD-mobile-touch-21, STD-mobile-touch-03, STD-when-to-animate-06 (changes started from the keyboard happen instantly).

title: How many text colors, and how far from pure black and white
questions: (questions the designer answers) How many text colors? Should the darkest text be pure black? Is secondary text a solid gray or the main text color made see-through? In dark mode, is text white or light gray?
options:
- **Three solid levels:** headings about 11% white, body 15 to 20%, subtext 30 to 40% [S-L19-039] (one video). For a pure gray that is about #1c1c1c, #262626 to #333333, and #4d4d4d to #666666 [inferred]. This matches Q-color-22's `solid-levels` default.
- **Two colors, the second by opacity:** the primary text color plus the same color at 45 to 70% opacity, with two "generally the maximum" [S-L19-057] (one video). This is Q-color-22's existing `opacity-levels` option.
- **Brand ink (new):** a very dark brand hue (a dark purple) for text instead of black; most text in the redesign is light gray or dark purple [S-L19-051].
- **Dark mode:** light grays for text because they are easier on the eyes than white, with pure white kept for the most important text such as the logo and the storage-used figure, and gray brightness lowered more aggressively than in light [S-L19-051]; "dim the text" [S-L19-039]. One video flips text to white [S-L19-085], which differs.
- Hierarchy uses size, weight and color together, not size alone [S-L19-057]; less important details such as file size and type go gray [S-L19-051].
visual effect: Three solid levels: a soft, professional hierarchy with no harsh black [inferred]. Two by opacity: minimal and consistent, and it blends with tinted surfaces (DC-L01-14). Brand ink: warm, branded and cohesive [inferred]. Light gray in dark with white reserved: easier on the eyes [S-L19-051], and the few white items pop [inferred].
depends on: DC-L19-02 (surfaces), DC-L19-03 (tint), Q-color-17 (contrast rule), Q-type-12 (weights).
affects: `color.text.primary`, `.secondary`, `.tertiary`, `.disabled`, `.inverse`, `color.icon.default`, placeholders and labels.
token encoding: $type color, solid aliases such as `color.text.primary` = `{color.neutral.light.12}`; the opacity variant uses the DTCG `alpha` component (DC-L01-14).
platform notes: Apple's label colors are vibrancy-aware and adapt on their own (DC-L01-14); the sources give nothing more.
accessibility constraints: Worked out from the sources' numbers [inferred]: on white, 11% gray is about 17:1, 20% about 12.6:1 and 40% (#666666) about 5.7:1, so all three solid levels pass 4.5:1, and still pass (5.3:1 or more) on a 96% page. By opacity, black at 45% on white is about 3.35:1 and at 50% about 4.0:1, both failing 4.5:1; 55% gives about 4.8:1, so about 54 to 55% is the lowest that passes. White at 45% on #121212 is about 4.5:1 (borderline) and on #1c1c1c about 4.4:1 (fails). Pure white on #121212 is about 18.7:1, the kind of very high contrast DC-L01-19 links to halation discomfort.
default: (default + heuristic) Default: keep Q-color-22's solid levels with secondary text passing 4.5:1 on the lowest surface. New: the darkest light-mode text is near-black rather than pure black [S-L19-039] [S-L19-051], and dark-mode text is light gray with pure white reserved for the most important text, such as the logo and a key figure [S-L19-051]. ([S-L19-057] differs: its primary text is plain black or white.) If opacity levels are chosen, the low end for body text is at least 55% in light and 50% in dark; lower values only for large text at 3:1 [inferred]. On the white-versus-light-gray split in dark mode, default to light gray with white reserved (two videos) over all white (one video).
maps to:
- Q-color-22: new option `brand-ink`; new floor on `opacity-levels` (55% in light, 50% in dark for body text); visual sample: the text ladder at 11%, 20% and 40% on white and on a 96% page, and the dark version with white only on the logo and one key number.
- Q-color-17: confirms the AA default (it catches the 45% case).
impact now / as it grows:
- Three solid levels: now, three tokens per mode. As it grows, every new surface (tinted panels, wells) needs each level re-checked.
- Two by opacity: now, the fewest tokens, and it adapts on any surface. As it grows, effective contrast drifts on tinted and colored panels, so each new surface pairing needs a check.
- Brand ink: now, cohesive. As it grows, a brand hue change re-tints all text.
standards: STD-visual-details-13 (over translucent surfaces use higher-contrast text, a slightly heavier weight and a little more letter spacing), STD-visual-details-09 (emphasize non-link text with weight or color, never an underline), STD-visual-details-29.

title: What draws the edge of a card: an opaque gray line or a see-through ring
questions: (questions the designer answers) What draws the edge of a card, a screenshot or the navigation bar: a solid light-gray line or a see-through dark ring? Where do edges have to be stronger?
options:
- **Opaque light-gray border:** roughly 85% white, not a thin black border; a subtle shadow alone is only slightly better than no edge [S-L19-039] (one video). That is about #d9d9d9, around 1.4:1 on white [inferred].
- **See-through ring:** an outer ring of gray 950 at 10% instead of a solid border on buttons, screenshots and the nav's bottom edge, because a solid border next to a shadow looks muddy; an inset ring on top of an image; soft "wells" of gray 950 at 5% behind screenshots (2.5% was too soft) [S-L19-103] (one video). If gray 950 is about #0a0a0a, the 10% ring is about 1.24:1 on white [inferred].
- **Subtle outline on nearly everything:** so the palette can stay pure white or near white, with pop-up shadows in a very light gray instead of transparent black [S-L19-059].
- **No stroke:** remove strokes that aren't needed, or dim them significantly if contrast is a worry [S-L19-045].
- What the engine has today (from the STD-visual-details-14 conflict note): opaque `color.border.subtle`, `.default` and `.strong` (#d2d2d2, #c9c9c9, #868686 in the default light theme) plus a 10%-alpha `color.shadow.ring`.
visual effect: Opaque: a flat, drawn edge [inferred] that can look muddy next to a shadow [S-L19-103]. See-through ring: a crisp edge that blends into the shadow [S-L19-103] and works on any background (DC-L01-27's reason for alpha) [inferred]. No stroke: the cleanest look, but surfaces must separate by tone or space [inferred].
depends on: DC-L19-02 (cards on the page), Q-depth-01 (shadows), Q-color-26 (see-through colors).
affects: `color.border.subtle`, `color.shadow.ring`, well backgrounds, cards, screenshot frames, the nav's bottom edge, dividers; not the functional borders of inputs.
token encoding: $type color with alpha, for example `color.shadow.ring` = `{"colorSpace": "srgb", "components": [0.04, 0.04, 0.04], "alpha": 0.1}` [inferred values]; decorative borders can alias the alpha neutrals (DC-L01-07, DC-L01-27).
platform notes: The sources give none. In forced-colors mode, rings drawn with box-shadow disappear (DC-L01-20), so a real border fallback is needed.
accessibility constraints: Decorative edges need no ratio. A control whose only boundary is its edge needs 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11); neither an 85% gray line (about 1.4:1) nor a 10% ring (about 1.2:1) is enough for inputs [inferred], so inputs keep `color.border.input` at 3:1. Provide a `forced-colors: active` border where the edge is a shadow ring (DC-L01-20).
default: (default + heuristic) Default: see-through ring for decorative edges (cards, screenshots, nav edge, popovers), which follows STD-visual-details-14 and [S-L19-103]; functional boundaries keep the 3:1 border token. The opaque 85% border [S-L19-039] stays available as an option, but it differs from STD-visual-details-14 and the standard wins. Heuristic: where a line meets a shadow, make the line see-through.
maps to:
- Q-color-23: new default wording "decorative edges use a see-through ring; interactive boundaries use the 3:1 border"; visual sample: card edges four ways (none and washed out, subtle shadow, 85% border, 10% ring) [S-L19-039] [S-L19-103].
- Q-color-26: confirms `alpha-neutrals`; adds the ring (10%) and well (5%) as named uses.
impact now / as it grows:
- Opaque border: now, a simple hex value. As it grows, the gray line looks dirty on tinted or image backgrounds, and each new surface color needs its own border value.
- See-through ring: now, one token works on every surface. As it grows, stacked translucent layers add up (a ring over a well over a tint), so composites need checking, and forced colors needs its fallback.
- No stroke: now, the cleanest. As it grows, dense screens lose structure unless tone steps carry it.
standards: STD-visual-details-14, STD-accessibility-motion-12 (under increased contrast, a defined contrasting border), STD-visual-details-26.

title: Chart colors for several series
block path: Foundations > Color > Data visualization > Categorical palette
questions: (questions the designer answers) When a chart has several lines or bars, how are their colors chosen: from the brand, from grays, or from a full spectrum? How is a comparison (last month) shown?
options:
- **Brand plus gray** (the current default, which already switches to `categorical-6-8` for dashboards): one brand color plus gray. The previous period drawn as a gray line behind the current one works well for business metrics [S-L19-075].
- **Brand ramp:** series in shades of the brand look too similar to tell apart [S-L19-039]; an opacity-only storage bar feels bland [S-L19-051].
- **Grays only:** "super lame" [S-L19-039] (taste).
- **Equal-lightness spectrum (new):** in OKLCH, fix lightness and chroma and step the hue by about 25 to 30 per series, so no color looks more neon than another (bright green versus bright blue) [S-L19-039] (one video). Eight series at that step cover about 175 to 210 degrees of hue [inferred].
- **Analogous or complementary for a few segments:** a storage bar colored with slightly rotated hues and a complementary yellow [S-L19-051].

Ordered palettes (Carbon): neighbors separate by lightness as well as hue [inferred from DC-L01-24's ordering].

affects: `color.chart.categorical.1` to `.8`, legends, tooltips, shaded maps, micro charts on KPIs.
